title: Holographic Dual of PT Symmetric BCFT
authors: Ryota Maeda, Nanami Nakamura, Tadashi Takayanagi
abstract: We present a holographic dual of a two dimensional conformal field theory with non-hermitian but Parity-Time (PT) symmetric boundary conditions, by applying the AdS/BCFT duality and by introducing an imaginary valued scalar field localized on an end-of-the-world brane. We find that as we increase the strength of the non-hermitian PT symmetric interactions, the system experiences a spontaneous PT symmetry breaking. We also consider its Wick rotated setup as a new quantum quenched state and show that its growth of entanglement entropy can be larger than the standard results obtained from standard Cardy states.
summary: This paper develops the holographic dual description for a 2D CFT with non-Hermitian $	ext{PT}$-symmetric boundary conditions using AdS/BCFT. Key findings include identifying the spontaneous breaking of $	ext{PT}$ symmetry and calculating entanglement entropy growth in quantum quench scenarios that surpass standard bounds. It provides a comprehensive theoretical framework linking gravity, field theory, and non-Hermitian physics.
main_problem: The research aims to find a holographic dual for a two-dimensional Conformal Field Theory (CFT) subjected to non-Hermitian but Parity-Time ($	ext{PT}$) symmetric boundary conditions.
main_result: The study demonstrates spontaneous $	ext{PT}$ symmetry breaking as the interaction strength increases, and it calculates entanglement entropy growth during quantum quenches that exceeds standard predictions.
method: The authors employ the AdS/BCFT duality, calculating on-shell actions in thermal ($	ext{TAdS}$) and black hole ($	ext{BTZ}$) geometries to determine system energy and phase transitions.
model_or_system: The model involves a $	ext{BCFT}$ defined on an interval with non-Hermitian boundary interactions localized via an End-of-the-World ($	ext{EOW}$) brane in the gravity dual. The analysis covers different phases, including thermal and black hole regimes.
key_observables: Energy ($E_T$), entanglement entropy growth rate ($\Delta S_A(t)$), and the boundary scalar source ($\Delta\phi$).
important_parameters: The deformation parameter $\Delta\phi$ controls the transition between $	ext{PT}$-symmetric and $	ext{PT}$-broken phases, with a critical point $\phi_c$.
main_assumptions: The analysis involves approximations for small deformations ($\Delta\phi \ll 1$) and requires extending calculations across different Riemann surfaces to map out the full parameter space.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy $E_T$ dependence on $\Delta\phi$, phase diagrams mapping system regimes, and plots showing how boundary parameters ($X, \Phi$) are calculated along specific contours in the complex plane.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the holographic dual across different phases (Thermal AdS vs. BTZ BH), determines critical points for symmetry breaking ($	ext{PT}$ breaking), and extends the analysis to quantum quench dynamics by Wick rotating the setup.
why_interesting: The connection between $	ext{PT}$-symmetry, non-Hermiticity, and holographic duality provides a powerful toolset for studying open quantum systems whose Hamiltonians are not standardly Hermitian, which is highly relevant to modern AMO physics.
